locator.section: 8 / Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (Random or hidden rearrangements)

evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.7, row 1, right branch (arrow labelled 'high energy'). The distonic gamma-radical cation undergoes beta-cleavage of the C2-C3 (alpha-beta) bond, giving the acetaldehyde enol radical cation CH2=CH-OH+. (m/z 44, drawn top-right with +. localized on oxygen) plus neutral 1-butene, which SEPARATE. Book draws 0 arc(s) on the 'high energy' arrow -- it prints only the two separated products, no fishhooks. All 5 electron moves are the implicit, balanced radical retro-ene cascade that produces them: the gamma-radical (move 1) and one C2-C3 electron (move 2) make the new C3=C4 pi bond; the other C2-C3 electron (move 3) and one C1=O pi electron (move 4) make the new C1=C2 pi bond; the remaining C1=O pi electron (move 5) becomes the oxygen radical. Text: at 70 eV this gamma-H/beta-cleavage 'gives mainly C2H4O+. (100%) + 1-C4H8', because IE(CH2=CHOH)=9.2 eV < IE(1-butene)=9.6 eV so the charge stays with the enol. DELOCALISATION: the enol radical cation is drawn/encoded with +. on O; the resonance partner .CH2-CH=O(+)H is the same ion. This is the net outcome also captured by Eq 8.5 (page 142).

Cross-link: MØD rule IMS_8_7_2 (rule_name 'Hydrogen exchange occring in a Ion-Molecule-Complex 8.7 row 1 high energy'). DFS: [C]1[C]2[C.]3[C]4[C]5[C]6([H]7){=}[O+]8[H]9 >> [C]1[C]2[C]3{=}[C]4.[C]5{=}[C]6([H]7)[O+.]8[H]9. VERIFIED consistent: the rule cleaves the bond between the radical-bearing carbon's beta neighbour (their C4-C5 = this record's C3-C2), forms the two new pi bonds (C3=C4 butene and C5=C6 enol in their numbering) and moves the radical from carbon to oxygen -- the same bond/charge/spin change encoded here. Their fragment [C]5{=}[C]6([H]7)[O+.]8[H]9 is the enol radical cation with +. on O, matching the drawn product.

The text prints 'C2H4O+. (100%)' for this 70 eV gamma-H/beta-cleavage product; 100% -> relative_intensity 1.0 (base peak). observed_mz 44.0257 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of C2H4O+. (electron-mass corrected); only the 100% is printed in the book.
